criteria.quote: Shellder makes pearls, then throws them away.
criteria.revision: Change the hook to: "Shellder turns trapped sand into a beautiful pearl—then spits it out because it gets in the way." This makes the contradiction and cause immediately clear using the research.

criteria.quote: Sand gets trapped inside Shellder's shell and mixes with body fluids.
How does Shellder turn trapped sand into something it immediately discards?
criteria.revision: Reframe the open loop as: "Why does Shellder treat the pearl it makes like clutter?" This delays the explanation while staying grounded in the fact that the pearl gets in the way and is discarded.

criteria.quote: The pearl gets in the way, so Shellder spits it out.
criteria.revision: Split the cause and consequence into separate beats: first, "The finished pearl gets in the way." Then reveal: "So Shellder spits it out and discards it." This makes the final action feel like an escalation instead of repeating the full premise.

criteria.quote: But the pearl gets in the way, so Shellder spits it out.
criteria.revision: Move this line later and make it the central reveal: "The pearl it made becomes an obstruction—so Shellder spits it out." The research supports the obstruction, while the delayed reveal changes the viewer's view of the pearl.

criteria.quote: Shellder makes pearls, then throws them away.
criteria.revision: Remove or rewrite the final "Its pearl-making ends with the finished pearl simply discarded" scene, since it repeats the opening and the previous scene. Use that beat only for the specific final action: "Shellder spits the pearl out and discards it."

criteria.quote: Shellder's beautiful pearl is not treasure to keep. It is an obstruction to spit out.
criteria.revision: Strengthen the ending through contrast without adding facts: "Shellder's process doesn't end with treasure—it ends when the beautiful pearl gets in the way and is spit out." This resolves the opening with the full cause-and-effect chain.

criteria.quote: Is Shellder a pearl maker or a pearl waster?
criteria.revision: Make the split more explicit: "Does making the pearl make Shellder a pearl maker—or does discarding it make Shellder a pearl waster?" Both sides remain grounded in the research.
